title: 换一棵树：B_f、Q_f 与 Q_l = −B_tᵀ
statement: 电路如图（U_s1 = 10 V，I_s5 = 1 A，R_1 = 2 Ω，R_2 = R_3 = 4 Ω，R_4 = R_5 = 2 Ω，R_6 = 8 Ω）。画有向图时把 U_s1 与 R_1 的串联看成一条支路（支路 1），把 R_5 与 I_s5 的并联看成一条支路（支路 5），其余每个电阻一条支路；结点编号 1、2、3、4（4 接地），支路编号与方向见下方的有向图。

这次选树 T = {4, 5, 6}（图中粗线），连支为 1、2、3。基本回路矩阵 B_f：每条连支对应一行（按连支编号从小到大），基本回路的方向取该连支的方向；支路 k 在回路 j 中且方向与回路一致时 b_jk = +1，相反时 −1，不在回路中为 0。基本割集矩阵 Q_f：每条树支对应一行（按树支编号从小到大），基本割集的方向取该树支的方向；支路 k 在割集 j 中且方向与割集一致时 q_jk = +1，相反时 −1，否则为 0。 先写 B_f，再用 Q_l = −B_tᵀ 写 Q_f。

questions.ask: b_15 = ?（连支 1 的基本回路中的支路 5）
q_12 = ?（Q_f 第 1 行即树支 4 的割集，支路 2）
questions.explain: Q_l = −B_tᵀ：q_12 = −b_24，B_f 第 2 行（连支 2）里支路 4 为 +1，所以 q_12 = −1。直接看：去掉树支 4，结点 2 单独一块，支路 2 进入结点 2，与割集方向（离开 2）相反。
q_33 = −b_36 = 0：连支 3 的基本回路 2→3→4→2 不经过树支 6，所以连支 3 也不在树支 6 的割集里。

questions.ask: 关于同一个图，下面哪个等式**不**成立？
choiceExplain: 成立：每个回路进出一个结点的次数相同（KCL 与 KVL 的正交性）。
成立：一个回路穿过一个割集的次数（按方向计）为零。
就是 A·B_fᵀ = 0 的转置，成立。
对：A 和 Q_f 都是“割集型”矩阵（A 的每一行就是包围一个结点的割集），它们的行空间相同，A·Q_fᵀ 一般不为零。

hints: 树 {4, 5, 6} 是以结点 4、3 为中心的“星形 + 一条边”：先确认它连通所有结点。
对每条连支沿树找回路。注意支路方向与回路走向是否一致。
Q_f 的连支部分不必另外找割集：Q_l = −B_tᵀ（B_f 中树支 4、5、6 的三列取负再转置）。
solution: **Q_f** 的树支部分为单位矩阵，连支部分 Q_l = −B_tᵀ：
**检查：** Q_f 第 1 行（树支 4 的割集）就是结点 2 的全部支路 {2, 3, 4}，方向离开结点 2：与 A 的第 2 行 (0, −1, 1, 1, 0, 0) 完全一样 ✓。

en.title: Another tree: B_f, Q_f and Q_l = −B_tᵀ
statement: The circuit is drawn below (U_s1 = 10 V, I_s5 = 1 A, R_1 = 2 Ω, R_2 = R_3 = 4 Ω, R_4 = R_5 = 2 Ω, R_6 = 8 Ω). In the graph, U_s1 in series with R_1 counts as one branch (branch 1), R_5 in parallel with I_s5 as one branch (branch 5), and each other resistor as one branch; the nodes are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 (4 is grounded) and the branch numbers and directions are those of the directed graph under the circuit.

This time choose the tree T = {4, 5, 6} (thick lines); the links are 1, 2, 3. Fundamental loop matrix B_f: one row per link (in ascending link number); each fundamental loop takes the direction of its link; b_jk = +1 if branch k is in loop j with the same direction, −1 if opposite, 0 if not in the loop. Fundamental cut-set matrix Q_f: one row per tree branch (ascending number); each fundamental cut-set takes the direction of its tree branch; q_jk = +1 if branch k is in cut-set j in the same direction, −1 if opposite, 0 otherwise. Write B_f first, then Q_f from Q_l = −B_tᵀ.

questions.ask: b_15 = ? (branch 5 in the loop of link 1)
questions.explain: Link 1: 4→1, then from 1 back to 4 along the tree: 1→3 (branch 6, same way) → 4 (branch 5, 3→4, same way): b_15 = b_16 = +1.
Link 2: 1→2, back from 2 to 1: 2→4 (branch 4, same way) → 3 (branch 5 reversed) → 1 (branch 6 reversed): b_25 = −1.

questions.ask: q_12 = ? (row 1 of Q_f = cut-set of tree branch 4, branch 2)
questions.explain: Q_l = −B_tᵀ: q_12 = −b_24; branch 4 is +1 in row 2 of B_f (link 2), so q_12 = −1. Directly: removing tree branch 4 isolates node 2; branch 2 enters node 2, against the cut-set (out of 2).
q_33 = −b_36 = 0: the loop of link 3 (2→3→4→2) does not use tree branch 6, so link 3 is not in its cut-set either.

questions.ask: Which equation does **not** hold for this graph?
choiceExplain: Holds: a loop leaves a node as often as it enters it (KCL/KVL orthogonality).
Holds: counted with direction, a loop crosses a cut-set zero times net.
This is the transpose of A·B_fᵀ = 0, so it holds.
Right: A and Q_f are both cut-set type matrices (each row of A is the cut-set around one node) with the same row space; A·Q_fᵀ is not zero in general.
questions.explain: Loops and cut-sets are orthogonal: A·B_fᵀ = 0, Q_f·B_fᵀ = 0.

hints: First check that {4, 5, 6} connects every node.
Find each link's loop along the tree, watching whether each branch runs with or against the loop.
No need to search the cut-sets: Q_l = −B_tᵀ (columns 4, 5, 6 of B_f, negated and transposed).
solution: **Q_f**: identity on the tree branches, Q_l = −B_tᵀ on the links:
**Check:** row 1 of Q_f (cut-set of tree branch 4) is all branches at node 2, {2, 3, 4}, pointing out of node 2: identical to row 2 of A, (0, −1, 1, 1, 0, 0) ✓.
